text: During a GNSS outage the chip-scale atomic clock (CSAC) shall keep the 95th-percentile timing error within 20 ns.
The CSAC shall hold the timing specification for at least 30 minutes after GNSS is denied.
The optical clock's timing error shall stay within 1 ns at every sample of the run.
The CSAC's timing error shall stay below 50 ns at every sample of the run.
The CSAC's Allan deviation at the shortest averaging time the run resolves shall not exceed 1e-10, computed with the IEEE 1139 power-law noise model and a validated Allan estimator.
capability: Frequency stability characterisation;IEEE-1139 power-law clock noise + flicker-FM floor

text: The clock filter shall pass its own statistical consistency check.
The horizontal protection level shall stay below the horizontal alert limit at every epoch.
Integrity shall be available at 95 % of epochs or more.
No epoch shall show misleading information: the vertical error shall stay inside the protection level.
In the chained jamming, spoofing and holdover mission, a spoofing alarm shall be raised within 30 minutes of the start.
In the chained mission the clock time error shall stay within its guard at every timeline step.
With low Earth orbit (LEO) augmentation the fused three-dimensional position error shall be 0.5 m root mean square (RMS) or better.
The LEO navigation message shall keep the signal-in-space range error (SISRE) within 30 cm RMS.
With 240 LEO satellites, precise point positioning (PPP) shall converge within 10 minutes.
The receiver housing shall carry the programme's identification label.
